stem: A developer builds a menu trigger with a clickable `<div>` instead of a `<button>`. Which change most directly restores keyboard and assistive technology support?

options.text: Replace the `<div>` with a native `<button>` element.
options.rationale: A native button is focusable, exposes a button role, and responds to Enter and Space without extra scripting.

options.text: Add `tabindex="0"` so the `<div>` can receive keyboard focus.
options.rationale: Tabindex makes the element focusable but does not give it a button role or make Enter and Space activate it.

options.text: Add a `title` attribute so the control has an accessible name.
options.rationale: A title may show a tooltip, but it is not a reliable accessible name and does not add keyboard behavior.

options.text: Add a `mouseover` event so the menu opens on hover.
options.rationale: Hover-only interaction excludes keyboard and touch users and does not make the trigger operable.

explanation: A native `<button>` is focusable, exposes a button role, and responds to Enter and Space by default. Adding `tabindex` alone makes an element focusable but does not give it a role or keyboard behavior; a `title` is not a reliable accessible name, and hover-only interaction excludes keyboard and touch users.

references.title: W3C WAI — Developing for Web Accessibility

author: Oxypteros
